MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing
  Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  October 14, 2025
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ruesch at
5:00 p.m., on October 14, 2025, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on October 9, 2025, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at the
Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray Community
and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ruesch

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  John R. Harper, Interim City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

RECESS AND RECONVENE MEETING

At the hour of 5:00 Mayor Ruesch recessed meeting. At the hour of 6:00 Mayor Ruesch reconvened
the meeting with four Council Members present and Council Member Goodell absent.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Vasquez

City Council Minutes  1  October 14, 2025
 PRESENTATIONS

P1. Adopted Headquarters Battalion of the 1st Marine Division Quarterly Recognition

  Mayor Ruesch presented certificates of commendation to the "Marine of the Quarter" Lance
  Corporal Sawyer Carleton, and "Noncommissioned Officers of the Quarter" Corporal Jmari
  Mellerson.

P2. Proclaim the Week of October 19 through 25, 2025 To Be National Friends of Libraries
  Week

  Mayor Ruesch presented proclamation to Pam Smith.

P3. Legislative Platform Update

  Received update from Cori Takkinen and Elisa Arcidiacono from Townsend Public Affairs.

P4. Housing Legislation Update

  Received update from Director of Community Development Larry Longenecker.

The Mayor announced that the City of Mission Viejo has officially partnered with the Netherlands
Olympic Committee, making Mission Viejo the Dutch team's home base as they prepare for the 2028
Los Angeles Olympics. This partnership is the result of years of community effort and vision, dating
back to when the city first learned about the 2028 Games. The Dutch chose Mission Viejo because of
the community’s welcoming spirit and strong support. In recognition, Mayor Ruesch invited various
community members, past and present—to stand and be acknowledged for their role in making this
partnership possible. The Dutch Olympic Committee expressed gratitude for the city's hospitality and
enthusiasm.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Sam Lewis, M.V.: Expressed heartfelt thanks to the Mayor and City Council for hosting the “Love Our
Schools” event. He highlighted the event’s powerful sense of unity, noting that while diversity was
present and appreciated, the real strength came from people coming together with a shared purpose—
to support the community and local schools. He shared how the event allowed him to meet new people
and form lasting friendships, emphasizing the importance of such opportunities to unite the community
beyond individual differences.

Lucy Harmor, M.V.: Introduced the character trait of the month: Respect. She explained that respect
involves admiration and high regard for others, and it includes many forms—such as self-respect,
respect for others, authority, property, the environment, and the country. Respect is shown through
actions like kindness, politeness, empathy, and listening. She emphasized the Golden Rule—treat
others the way you want to be treated—and shared her personal example of showing respect by picking
up trash to protect the environment.

City Council Minutes  2  October 14, 2025
 Tom Moore, M.V.: Expressed concern over the long-standing issue of fragmented commercial property
ownership at Marguerite Parkway and La Paz Road. He referenced the 2007 ULI report and the city’s
subsequent Vision Plan, noting that despite years of planning and documentation, the core issue remains
unresolved. He criticized past city leadership and staff for not addressing key legal and logistical
questions. He also commented on a recent council meeting, commending the District 3 councilmember
for raising questions about the financial implications of the city’s agreement with the Dutch Olympic
Committee. While supportive of the Dutch partnership, he emphasized the need for fiscal responsibility
and greater council accountability.

Jessica Jensen, M.V.: Jessica, representing Pack 703, highlighted the pack’s growth since 2021 and
requested continued city support for outreach. Sedric Campbell, Executive Director of Scouting
America, shared that the organization serves over 46,000 youth in Orange County, including 1,000 in
the Saddleback District—25% from Mission Viejo. Both thanked the city for supporting youth
development through Scouting. Both thanked the city for supporting youth development through
Scouting

June Anderson, M.V.: She thanked the City Council for its principled stance in opposing Proposition
50, calling it a threat to fair elections and representative government. She urged residents to learn more
about the measure and join in defending voter rights. Lastly, she congratulated the city on receiving a
million-dollar grant for the Oso Creek Trail and expressed interest in how the funds will benefit the
Casta del Sol community.

Karen Warren, M.V.: She thanked the Mayor, City Council, and especially Councilmember Trish
Kelley for opposing Proposition 50, calling it a threat to voter rights and election transparency. She
urged residents to recognize the measure as a power grab and vote “No” to protect representative
government. The comment also honored the legacy of Charlie Kirk, a tireless warrior for the importance
of defending election integrity.

Carolyn Gatto, M.V.: She thanked Captain Ivins for arranging police presence during a peaceful protest
on October 1. She raised several questions about the Netherlands Olympic Team’s training in Mission
Viejo, including who is covering living expenses, where athletes will stay, and whether public access
to the Marguerite Aquatics Complex will be affected. She also inquired about the city's spending to
welcome the team. Lastly, the speaker voiced support for Proposition 50, describing it as a necessary
response to the inept administration in Washington and urged others to vote “Yes.”

Peggy O’Neill, M.V.: She emphasized the importance of restoring checks and balances among the three
branches of government, criticizing Congress for ceding too much power to the executive branch. She
urged support for Proposition 50, describing it as a temporary but necessary measure to counter partisan
redistricting efforts in other states, particularly Texas. Lastly, she argued that Prop 50 would help
preserve fair representation and uphold the founders’ vision of a balanced government.

Cathy Palmer, M.V.: She raised concerns and questions regarding the Los Osos Center project,
including when the public will receive an update, the impact of ongoing lawsuits, and the cost of
consultant studies. They noted that the city has paused the project to allow for further due diligence and
to explore a potential public-private partnership. She also inquired about the RFQ process for the former
Stein Mart building and suggested the city consider mixed-use developments such as residential above
retail—for underperforming shopping centers.
City Council Minutes  3  October 14, 2025
 Lynn Holmes, M.V.: She expressed disappointment with the City Council’s public opposition to
Proposition 50, urging a more balanced presentation of both sides to allow residents to make informed
decisions. She argued that Prop 50 is a temporary, voter-approved response to federal overreach and
partisan redistricting. She also called for greater focus on revitalizing downtown Mission Viejo, citing
vacant buildings and underused spaces. She encouraged the city to invest in beautification, attract new
businesses, and prepare the area to make a positive impression—especially ahead of the Netherlands
Olympic Team’s arrival.

Stacy Holmes, M.V.: Voiced support for Proposition 50, favoring redistricting maps ratified by voters
over those drawn unilaterally by state legislatures, as seen in Texas. He criticized the City Council for
not addressing partisan redistricting in other states and highlighted the disproportionate federal tax
contributions made by California. Argued that Prop 50 is a temporary, voter-approved measure to
ensure fairness and balance in congressional representation and called for stronger advocacy from
California’s elected officials to protect the state’s interests.

Kristen Wilcox, M.V.: She questioned the Mayor’s decision to maintain the current voting structure,
despite public input favoring randomized, staggered district terms and more seats on the general
election ballot. She criticized the Council for disregarding resident feedback and highlighted
Councilmember Vasquez’s data showing higher voter turnout in general elections. She also expressed
frustration over the Council’s decision to lower flags in honor of Charlie Kirk, stating it appeared to
prioritize presidential directives over your constituents.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent calendar outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  5  October 14, 2025
   Received written report from Council Member Bucknum.

CITY MANAGER REPORTS

City Manager Lister provided an update on the Los Osos project, noting that while the original
development plans were attractive, several challenges have emerged since the project began around
2017–2019. These include the changing market conditions and major store closures (e.g., Big Lots,
Michaels, CVS), legal complications due to outdated CC&Rs from the 1970s, rising interest and
construction costs, and limited interest from potential development partners. She stated that a Request
for Qualifications (RFQ) has been issued to attract a broader range of potential partners and explore
innovative development options, including public-private partnerships or possible property sales. The
RFQ focuses on identifying experienced partners, not detailed proposals (which would come in a later
RFP phase). She indicated that the Responses are due by October 17.

Assistant City Manager Hill gave a progress report on the CAL FIRE grant-funded wildfire mitigation
efforts. He stated that the crews are actively clearing vegetation and creating defensible space in the
Wilderness Glen area, including behind homes near Trabuco and Via Noveno with expanded clearance
that CAL FIRE approved for an additional 70 feet of clearance (totaling 170 feet) behind homes on Via
Noveno and Via Santiago. Environmental surveys have been completed, and CEQA documentation is
expected to be finalized by the end of October. He stated that the next step will be to continue along
Los Alisos to Trabuco and into nearby open spaces, including behind a cul-de-sac area. Future Funding
is in the second-round CAL FIRE grant application which was submitted on October 1 for the
maximum amount of $950,000, aiming to address fire hazards like dead palm trees in open spaces.
Lastly, he said the goats were used successfully for vegetation management in Jeronimo Open Space.
The effort was effective in rough terrain, and two baby goats were born during the project.

CITY ATTORNEY REPORTS

Interim City Attorney Harper responded to a public comment made earlier regarding the ongoing
litigation across the street. He said the status of ongoing litigation cannot be discussed publicly due to
the Brown Act, which protects litigation privilege. These matters are handled in closed session with the
City Council to avoid waiving that privilege. Public discussion of litigation could compromise legal
protections.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

15. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
  presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell said they had a very full schedule during the recent visit from our Dutch
partners, and a lot took place over the course of their stay. Since then, several questions have come up
regarding logistics and financial arrangements. While I can answer some of them, I’d prefer not to
City Council Minutes  6  October 14, 2025
 provide incomplete or potentially inaccurate information. With that in mind, I’d like to request that Mr.
Nix provide a report at our next meeting to clarify: How the visit was organized and conducted, who
covered which expenses, details of the agreement, including the $1 million commitment from the Dutch
delegation, and any city-sponsored events or contributions. He understood that the Dutch delegation is
covering their own expenses, including lodging and meals, as outlined in the agreement. They hosted
one community event, which was a barbecue at the lake and the city may be covering some
transportation costs in the long term, as previously agreed. Overall, it seems to be a fair and balanced
partnership. Council Member Goodell indicated that during their visit, they also held a special chair
dedication ceremony at Lakeside Park (Alicia & Marguerite) in memory of Jeff Lauder, a longtime
resident, community leader, and one of the original advocates for the lake. Jeff had a meaningful
connection with the Dutch team, and their executives joined us to honor him at the event. On a personal
note, he missed a few of the weekend activities because he and his wife welcomed their seventh
grandchild, Ruby Lee Goodell, born Friday at Mission Hospital. This is their sixth granddaughter, and
they are thrilled.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley attended Coffee Conversations with Senator Catherine Blakespear, who
shared updates from Sacramento and continues to advocate for our city. She also attended two Eagle
Scout projects, one at Minaya Park for fence repainting and cleanup, and another at Crucero Park,
which is under renovation. Thanks to Bryan Zahn for his great work with the Scouts for their
contributions are a real asset to Mission Viejo. She attended the Jeff Lauder Chair Dedication at
Lakeside Park, a touching tribute joined by members of Team Netherlands. On October 3, she was at
the Dutch agreement signing at Lake Mission Viejo, a proud moment for our city. On October 5, the
city hosted the first Mission Viejo Track Meet with Team Netherlands. On October 11, she had a full
day with: Love Our Schools volunteer event, Fire Station 24 Open House, and the Animal Shelter Fall
Fest & Pumpkin Patch. Council Member Kelley also attended the League of California Cities
Conference in Long Beach, great sessions and networking. Looking ahead, she reminded residents not
to miss the Walk Against Drugs this Saturday, starting at 8:00 a.m. at Mission Viejo High School,
followed by a fair at Oso Viejo Park. She said it’s a great community event for all ages. Lastly, she said
there’s always something happening in Mission Viejo so check the city website and get involved!

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez attended Coffee Conversations with Senator Catherine Blakespear and
appreciated the update on her work in Sacramento. The next evening, she went to the Movie in the
Park at Napoli Park and it was a lively crowd for Lilo & Stitch, and her youngest had a great time with
her friends. On September 28, she attended Beats, Bids & Boogie for MS at the Norman P. Murray
Center, a great event with an impressive auction turnout. She also attended the memorial service for
our former City Attorney on October 3, which was a meaningful opportunity to meet his family and
offer condolences. That same day, she supported her daughter’s school Book Fair, and the next day,
she participated in the city’s E-Waste event. Over the weekend, she visited her oldest at Cal State Long
Beach for a family event with games, food, and a women’s volleyball game. She also attended
a memorial for a former neighbor and friend who passed away from Alzheimer’s. Later that week, she
also attended the League of California Cities Conference in Long Beach. she gathered some great ideas
she hopes to share with Elaine and Jerry soon.

City Council Minutes  7  October 14, 2025
 Finally, her family took a short trip to Sonoma where they visited the Charles M. Schulz
Museum (which we call the Snoopy Museum) and the Jelly Belly Factory. Her youngest had a blast
and is still drawing what she saw there. It was a quick but memorable trip, and she made it back to
school Monday morning!

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum attended the Jeff Lauder Chair Dedication, a touching tribute to someone
instrumental in building our Dutch partnership. It was meaningful to see his family and members of the
Dutch delegation there. The Dutch agreement signing was a success, and their delegation was
impressed by the city’s hospitality and facilities. This partnership benefits our residents, businesses,
and local economy especially as we look ahead to the Olympics. The Love Our Schools event was
fantastic as she helped with painting at Silverado and Montevideo and appreciated the community
turnout. She also stopped by the Animal Services Fall Fest and the OCFA Open House with her dog,
Bert. She attended Saddleback College’s Foundation fundraiser at their Advanced Technology Center,
an impressive event showcasing their top-tier programs. Looking ahead, she pointed out upcoming
events next Saturday: Night Market, Pet Vaccine Clinic, Prescription Take-Back Day, Pumpkin Dive,
and the Día de los Muertos Festival. Lastly, she supports efforts to improve neglected business centers
and appreciates the community’s input. Also, she clarified that when the President orders flags at half-
staff, the city follows that tradition.

Mayor Ruesch

Mayor Ruesch stated that one of the great things about serving as Mayor is knowing that even if you
can’t attend every event, someone else is always there representing the city. He appreciates that
teamwork. He highlighted the following: The Track Meet Councilmember Kelley mentioned was the
first since COVID. It was once a popular event, and it’s great to see it returning, the final Symphony
on the Go performance was held at Melinda Park, which was always a fantastic experience. Our
partnership with Pacific Symphony is something special. He recently met with Simon Property
Group as part of his goal to reconnect with major businesses in the city. He indicated that with the
Olympics on the horizon, the city is working to build a more cohesive business community that can
share in the excitement and opportunities ahead. He closed his comments with the following thought:
“What’s your plan? We all have goals, whether it’s a job, health, family, or something else. But how
do you get there? Think of your goal as a mountain peak. You need a plan, a roadmap to reach it. Break
it down into steps. Make it measurable. Stay focused. And when you reach that summit, celebrate your
success. As I often say: If you don’t know where you’re going, maybe you’ve already arrived. So
tomorrow, write down your goal and take that first step.”

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 8:08 pm., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session, Mayor
Ruesch adjourned the meeting in memory of Ginny Taylor, to Tuesday, October 14, 2025, at 5:00 p.m.
Ginny was a dedicated volunteer with the Senior Core of Retirees (SCOR) who served the City of
Mission Viejo for 20 years.
